neighbours.label: the start of a broadcaster or media / telecom company name after 'on' or 'at': W-call-sign stations (WPHL, WGBH), Westwood One, Verizon, ad agencies; the - pole is audience-ratings talk (Nielsen, Arbitron)
fire: Her morning programme is carried every weekday on WNYC Radio in New York.
He started out reading the weather at WTVJ Television in Miami.
The interview was broadcast last night on Westwood One Radio.
She left the newspaper to become a producer at WBEZ Radio in Chicago.
After college he sold airtime at WKRC Television in Cincinnati.
The debate will be heard live on WAMU Radio at eight.
He spent a decade as an account director at Wunderman before starting his own agency.
The long-running quiz show still airs on WHYY Television in Philadelphia.
quiet: Her morning class is held every weekday at Wellesley College near Boston.
He started out stacking shelves at Walmart in a suburb of Miami.
The interview was held last night on Westminster Bridge in the rain.
She left the newspaper to become a teller at Wells Fargo in Chicago.
After college he sold tractors at a dealership in Cincinnati.
The debate will be held on Wednesday at eight.
He spent a decade as a design director at Whirlpool before starting his own firm.
The long-running farmers market still opens on Walnut Street in Philadelphia.

notes: Card: peak ' W' x5, ' West' x4 (Westwood One), ' on', ' Ad', ' Verizon'; examples are radio/TV stations and media or telecom employers. Probes: 'on WGBH Radio' 0.34, 'at Ogilvy' 0.26, 'at Ericsson and later at Sprint' 0.21; 'at Boeing ... Ford' 0.04, 'on Channel 9' 0.01, 'Comcast' early in the sentence 0.00. Probes sit near the 0.20 line, so the median is uncertain.
